ruleset.name: lattice-unused
ruleset.description:
The unused-private-member gate. Deliberately two rules and nothing else.
PMD is here for exactly one job the other Java gates cannot do: telling us a private field or method is declared and never used. Both of the gates that look like they should have caught it were measured and do not. Checkstyle ships no field-level unused check at all (the pinned version has UnusedLocalVariable, which covers locals only). SpotBugs, run over main and test sources at its lowest threshold and highest effort with exclusions off, reported nothing for either of the two real cases - not the unused instance field, and not the unused constant. The constant case is the structural one: javac inlines a compile-time constant, so a bytecode tool cannot reliably tell "never used" from "used and inlined". That is why this check has to read source, and reading source is what PMD does.
Keeping the ruleset to these two rules is the point, not laziness. PMD is a second static-analysis engine sitting next to SpotBugs, which is in tension with the one-engine-per-job rule; the tension is acceptable only while PMD stays scoped to the job SpotBugs demonstrably cannot do. Adding general-purpose PMD categories here would turn it into an overlapping second bug-finder, and the two engines would start disagreeing about the same code. Add a rule only with the same deliberation any other gate change gets.
A violation is an error, not a warning: failOnViolation is on in the pom, because a warning in a build this size is a warning nobody reads.
